confidence_notes: I converted GBP to USD at about 1.31 USD per GBP, which is an estimate and not from a search. It roughly matches the GBP/EUR cross implied by the RBA's euro and US dollar rates in the search summary. Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from aggregated, crowd-sourced Cardiff figures returned by search. Those sources give a domestic pint at about £4.90–£5.31, a cappuccino at about £3.45–£3.50, an inexpensive meal at about £15 and a mid-range three-course meal for two at about £65–£66. The cocktail anchor is less certain: the only aggregate was about £9 from a small, older sample (October 2025), and venue deals are lower. I used about £9.75 to reflect July 2026 pricing. I found no aggregate price for a glass of wine. I estimated about £7 for a 175 ml glass, based on the usual UK markup over a pint and my general knowledge. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for the July 2026 summer season, adjusted for event-driven demand around the Principality Stadium. I did not search for accommodation prices or check them against live listings. The FX observation (0.6720 USD per AUD on 18 November 2026) came from a web-search summary that credited it to the RBA's exchange-rate page. I did not open the RBA page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Cardiff-specific aggregated cost-of-living data for food and drink. Accommodation is benchmarked against other mid-sized UK regional cities that host events, such as Bristol, Newcastle and Liverpool. Cardiff is generally a little cheaper than Bristol and well below London.
